messages.content: Write a customer testimonial section for the website of a log aggregation service. Around 200 words.

Names and companies below are placeholders — swap in real, approved quotes before this ships.

---

## What people tell us

> "We had 14 services writing logs to 14 different places. Finding one request across all of them meant SSH, `grep`, and a lot of swearing. Now it's one query box. The first week we used it, we found a retry loop that had been quietly burning $900 a month in egress since March."
>
> **Priya Raghavan** — Staff SRE, Northbound Freight

> "I care about one number: how long it takes to answer 'what happened at 3:14 a.m.' Used to be forty minutes. It's about ninety seconds. Our on-call rotation stopped feeling like a punishment."
>
> **Marcus Oyelaran** — Engineering Manager, Tessellate

> "The retention pricing is what sold my finance team. We keep 90 days hot and two years cold, and we still spend less than we did on the self-hosted cluster nobody wanted to maintain. I have not thought about disk pressure in a year."
>
> **Dana Whitfield** — CTO, Larkspur Health

> "Setup was an afternoon. One agent, one config file, and our existing dashboards kept working."
>
> **Tom Iwanaga** — Platform Engineer, Rally Six

---

~205 words. The claims are all specific and checkable on purpose — swap the numbers for ones your real customers will stand behind, since made-up metrics in a testimonial are the fastest way to lose the credibility the section exists to build.

Change nothing else, and keep the same length and purpose.
